items.title: Samādhāya Mano Hṛdi — heart-centering before japa
items.instruction: Sit. Place hand on heart. Take 3 breaths, feeling heart area. Tell mind: 'Mind, we are going to the heart now.' Then chant from the heart, not the head. When mind drifts to thinking, gently return it to the heart.

items.title: Bhurijana's Saṅkalpa — the doable request
items.instruction: When the mind is wild, ask only: 'Hear just ONE mantra completely.' Then: 'Just one more.' Make the request small enough that the mind can comply. The mind eventually embraces the Name through patient repetition.
items.source: HG Bhurijana Prabhu, Japa: Nine Keys from the Śikṣāṣṭaka

items.title: The P.A.U.S.E. method for anger
items.instruction: When anger arises during the day: Pause (don't act). Acknowledge ('anger has arisen,' not 'I am angry'). Understand (what desire was frustrated?). Surrender ('Krishna, please help me respond'). Engage wisely. 30 seconds prevents hours of regret.
items.source: Nama-Tattva publication Sec. 2.7; HH Radhanath Swami

items.title: Higher Taste — the antidote to kāma
items.instruction: Don't fight a desire; cultivate something higher. Tonight before sleep, read one Krishna pastime — even five minutes. Material taste diminishes when spiritual taste arises (BG 2.59 — paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate).

items.title: Hear each of the 32 syllables
items.instruction: Hare Krishna mahā-mantra has 16 words, 32 syllables. Today, chant slowly enough to hear every syllable clearly. If you cannot hear them, slow down. The mouth chants for the ear's benefit.
items.source: HG Mahatma Prabhu; NOI verse 1 purport

items.title: Tṛṇād Api meditation before japa
items.instruction: Before the first round, sit and recall: 'I am lower than the straw. Whatever capacity I have to chant is borrowed from guru and Krishna. None of it is mine.' This is not performance — it is the actual qualification for chanting.

items.title: The Mānadena practice
items.instruction: Morning: name three devotees by name and one quality you appreciate in each. During the day, when envy arises, find three good qualities in that person. Evening: pray for the advancement of three named devotees.

items.title: Anti-Mada morning routine
items.instruction: Before the mirror this morning: 'I am a tiny jīva, completely dependent on Krishna's mercy. Whatever abilities I have are borrowed from Him. Without His grace, I cannot even digest my food. Let me not be puffed up today.'

items.title: Eternal Investment — anti-lobha
items.instruction: Tonight ask: 'Where did I invest more today — material or eternal? Money saved is lost at death. Japa chanted goes with me. What eternal assets did I create today?'

items.title: Cold water on the face before japa
items.instruction: Splash cold water on the face before sitting. This is a small act of pratyāhāra — it alerts the senses, signals the body that practice is beginning, and dispels morning dullness immediately.

items.title: The 4-Step Technique
items.instruction: (1) Saṅkalpa — 'hear just one mantra.' (2) Neglect the mind when it rebels. (3) Take shelter — accept the Name as Krishna Himself. (4) Await mercy — don't demand. Let the mind embrace the Name.
items.source: HG Bhurijana Prabhu, VIHE Holy Name Retreats

items.title: Diamond Throne meditation during japa
items.instruction: Within the heart, create a throne of jewels. Place Krishna there. Wash His lotus feet. Dress Him. Offer Him food. Do all this within while you chant outside. The hands offer; the tongue chants; the heart serves.

items.title: Brāhma-muhūrta — the sattvic window
items.instruction: 1.5 hours before sunrise, the mode of goodness predominates and the world is still. The Name lands cleanly in a mind not yet disturbed by the day. If you can begin then — even by 10 minutes earlier than usual — the rounds settle faster.

items.title: Sattvic dinner — light and early
items.instruction: Tonight: light vegetarian dinner, eaten by 7 PM if possible. Heavy, late, or rajasic food disturbs the early-morning mind. Less in the stomach tonight means more clarity tomorrow. Eat as if to chant tomorrow.

items.title: Today's Two Doors check
items.instruction: After japa, ask one question: 'Did I chant through Door 1 (mechanical pronunciation, no prema) or Door 2 (calling out with love, Krishna taking notice)?' One word answer. Build awareness, no shame.
items.source: HH Sacinandana Swami, Learning to Chant with Devotion

items.title: BUDDHYĀ Analysis for kāma
items.instruction: When a strong desire arises, use intelligence (buddhyā): 'This desire has arisen many times. Each time I satisfied it, did it bring lasting peace? No. Therefore, redirect the energy.' Then chant one focused round.

items.title: Pratyāhāra through engagement
items.instruction: Don't suppress the senses. Redirect them: ears to kirtana, eyes to deity darshan or sastra, tongue to prasadam, touch to deity service. Yoga's pratyāhāra meets bhakti's seva. Engagement IS the discipline.

items.title: Three-Step meditation before japa
items.instruction: (1) 'I am part of Krishna.' (2) 'He is my only master.' (3) 'Today let me reform my tendency to remain absent.' Slow recitation, with feeling, before beginning the first round.

items.title: Sleep before midnight
items.instruction: Hours of sleep BEFORE midnight are about twice as restorative as hours after. Tonight, aim for sleep by 10:45 PM. The morning chanter is made the night before.

items.title: No screens after 8 PM
items.instruction: What enters the eyes and ears before sleep strongly shapes morning consciousness. Tonight: no news, no social media, no entertainment after 8 PM. Read sastra instead, or chant softly. The mind sleeps in what it last touched.

items.title: Anti-Moha morning clarity (5 min)
items.instruction: Five minutes, eyes closed: 'I am not this body. I am eternal servant of Krishna. Today my purpose is to serve Him. Everything else is temporary arrangement.' Then begin japa with clear consciousness.

items.title: Tolerance Like a Tree
items.instruction: Visualization: I am a tall, strong tree. Someone cuts my branches — I give them wood for their fire. Someone scorches me in summer — I give them cooling shade. Apply: today, when someone 'cuts' me, give them something beneficial in return.

items.title: Today's Enemy Check
items.instruction: Before japa, 30 seconds: 'Which of the six enemies is loudest in me right now? Kāma? Krodha? Lobha? Moha? Mada? Mātsarya?' Name it. Offer that enemy specifically to Krishna in this round.

items.title: Posture is offered too
items.instruction: Sit straight. Spine erect. Cross-legged on the floor or upright in a chair — both are fine. Hands in mudra over the bead bag. The form of the body is also offered to Krishna. Slouching invites tamas.

items.title: Death meditation (1 min weekly)
items.instruction: Once this week, sit for one minute with this thought: 'This body will be ash or worm food. All positions, possessions, relationships — temporary. What remains? Only my relationship with Krishna.' Sobering. Re-orienting.

items.title: Sunday weekly reset
items.instruction: Sunday: take stock. Which enemies were loudest this past week? Which offense surfaced most? Choose one specific countermeasure for the coming week — not a vague resolution, a concrete practice.

items.title: Evening one-word reflection
items.instruction: Before sleep, one word for today's chanting: 'attentive,' 'wandering,' 'dry,' 'sweet,' 'rushed,' 'present.' One word. No judgment. Awareness builds over months.
items.source: HG Mahatma Prabhu; Saturday observe practice

items.title: Offense #1 vigilance
items.instruction: Mātsarya — envy of devotees — is the most subtle enemy and the cause of offense #1 (satāṁ nindā). When you catch yourself criticizing a devotee in your mind, STOP. Find one quality in them to appreciate. Convert criticism to prayer.

items.title: Water before japa
items.instruction: Sip water before beginning. A dry throat invites a wobbling voice; a wobbling voice invites a wandering mind. Small disciplines protect large practices.

items.title: Pre-japa cold splash + tulasi
items.instruction: Cold water on the face (alerts senses), then if Tulasi-maharani is near, offer respects before starting. Her presence sweetens the Name. Two acts; thirty seconds; the threshold is crossed.
